messages.author: 348b0b48aabf75ca
messages.subject: RE: tidyLPA question
parts:
Dear Joyce,

 

I can’t see the pictures you sent to Joshua, but generally, non-normality IS the assumption when conducting latent profile analysis! The official name of latent profile analysis is “mixture modeling”. That means: a mixture of several (normal) distributions.

 

To compare models, I’d recommend focusing on the BIC. The dev version of tidyLPA also gives you a bootstrapped LRT, and applies the automatic hierarchical process to give one recommended number of classes based on several fit indices. Get it by running: library(devtools); install_github(“cjvanlissa/tidyLPA”)

 

Best,

Caspar

Dear Joyce,

 

Depends on the package used for estimation! Mplus uses FIML by default. Mclust does not have a way to handle missing data. My version of the package has a function, single_imputation(), which does parametric or random forests-based single imputation, which you can do before passing the data to Mclust!

Caspar

Dear Joyce,

 

I can’t see the pictures you sent to Joshua, but generally, non-normality IS the assumption when conducting latent profile analysis! The official name of latent profile analysis is “mixture modeling”. That means: a mixture of several (normal) distributions.

 

To compare models, I’d recommend focusing on the BIC. The dev version of tidyLPA also gives you a bootstrapped LRT, and applies the automatic hierarchical process to give one recommended number of classes based on several fit indices. Get it by running: library(devtools); install_github(“cjvanlissa/tidyLPA”)

 

Best,

>> Not sure if this is a data problem. The bsfdata set has about 700 observations and 6,000 variables although I'm only interested in running LPA on 12 of the variables. Any thoughts on how I could address the error messages?

You should select the variables you are going to use first; not just because the imputation can take a long time without that (especially for the missForest imputation, which is superior, imputation on such a large dataset would take days).

 

My thoughts are that one of the 6000 variables has no variance, or is not numerical.

Caspar
